column4: Raise your hand if you've ever driven around the block three, four, five times just looking for a parking spot. Now keep it up if you were late because of it. That frustration — that wasted time, that wasted fuel — happens to millions of people every single day. In fact, the average urban driver wastes over 17 hours a year just searching for parking. That's two full workdays. Gone. We decided that's not acceptable. So we built SpotHawk.

column3: Quantify parking pain: congestion, wasted fuel, driver frustration, city costs. Make it visceral.
column4: Parking is a broken system. Cities lose billions in productivity each year because drivers are circling blocks instead of reaching their destination. Up to 30% of urban traffic at any given moment is just people looking for parking. That means more congestion, more emissions, more stress — and zero value created. Existing solutions like parking sensors and painted lines are static, expensive to install, and cover only a fraction of the city. The data simply doesn't exist in real time. Until now.

column3: Introduce the product clearly: drone fleet + CV + real-time app. One sentence pitch + key differentiators.
column4: SpotHawk is a drone-powered real-time parking intelligence platform. We deploy autonomous drones over urban areas, capture live aerial footage, and use computer vision to detect exactly which spots are free — right now. Drivers get that information instantly through our mobile app, with predictive guidance on where spots are likely to open near them. One sentence: SpotHawk turns the sky into your parking sensor.

column3: Simple 3-step visual: Drone scans → AI detects → Driver navigates. Keeps it concrete.
column4: The system works in three steps. First — our drone fleet continuously patrols designated urban zones, capturing aerial imagery on a rolling basis. Second — our computer vision engine processes that footage in real time, identifying occupied and free spots with high accuracy. Third — that data flows straight into our app, where drivers see a live map and get routed to the nearest available spot. Simple, fast, and scalable to any city without laying a single sensor in the ground.

column3: TAM/SAM/SOM or city-scale numbers. Shows the opportunity size.
column4: The global smart parking market is valued at over 5 billion dollars today and is projected to reach 11 billion by 2028. Our initial focus is mid-to-large European cities — think Sofia, Prague, Vienna — where parking density is high and infrastructure investment is constrained. In Sofia alone there are an estimated 300,000 daily parking searches. Even capturing 5% of that market at a modest subscription price puts us at a strong revenue base from a single city. The opportunity scales directly with urbanization.

column3: 2–3 persona cards (Urban Commuter, Tourist/Visitor, City Municipality) with goals, pain points, and what they'll pay for.
column4: We serve three core personas. First — Martin, the daily commuter. He drives into the city center every morning, parks for 8 hours, and is perpetually late because the first 15 minutes are spent circling. He'll pay for reliability. Second — Elena, the weekend visitor. She's meeting friends in a neighborhood she doesn't know, parking is a mystery, and she just wants to be told where to go. She's our pay-per-use customer. Third — the City Transport Department. They want congestion data, usage analytics, and a smarter city — and they have procurement budgets to match.

column3: Why customers will actually buy this — not just what it does
column4: but the specific gain/pain relief per segment.
column5: For the commuter — we give back time. No more circling, no more stress, no more being late. For the visitor — we remove the unknown. You arrive, you park, done. For the municipality — we provide live urban mobility data they simply cannot get today without expensive ground infrastructure. And across all segments, SpotHawk reduces the number of cars searching at any moment — which means less congestion and lower emissions citywide. We're not just a convenience app. We're urban infrastructure, delivered from the air.

column3: Competitor landscape (Google Maps parking, ParkMobile, sensors-based systems) vs. SpotHawk — what makes you uniquely better.
column4: Current alternatives fall into two camps. Apps like Google Maps or ParkMobile show you paid lots — static, pre-listed locations. Ground sensor systems like Siemens or Kapsch are accurate but cost tens of thousands per street to install and years to deploy. SpotHawk sits in neither camp. We cover the entire city surface — streets, lots, informal zones — with zero ground infrastructure. Our drones can be redeployed to new zones in hours. We're faster to deploy, cheaper per square meter of coverage, and the only solution that sees the full picture from above.

column3: Subscriptions, pay-per-use, B2B/municipal contracts, advertising. Show unit economics if possible.
column4: We monetize across four streams. Drivers subscribe monthly or yearly for premium real-time access and predictive features — think 3 to 5 euros a month. Occasional users pay per session. Municipalities and parking operators pay us for data feeds and analytics through B2B contracts — this is our highest-value stream. And locally, businesses can sponsor highlighted zones in the app. Our cost structure is drone fleet, cloud infrastructure, and personnel. As the fleet scales and routes are optimized, unit costs drop and margins improve significantly.

column3: Key findings from testing: what worked, what was validated, metrics (task completion, satisfaction scores, quotes from testers).
column4: We tested our prototype with 14 users across two rounds. The core finding: 92% of testers said they would use SpotHawk over their current approach. Average task completion time for finding and navigating to a spot was under 40 seconds. The biggest pain point we uncovered and fixed was map clutter — users wanted a cleaner default view with filtering. One tester said, and I quote: 'This is exactly what I've needed every time I drive into the city.' That kind of validation tells us the problem is real and our solution resonates.
